    82: def choose_most_severe_status(statuses: List[str]) -> str:
    83:     if not statuses:
    84:         return HEALTHY
    85: 
    86:     valid_statuses = [
    87:         status for status in statuses
    88:         if status in GOVERNANCE_SEVERITY_ORDER
    89:     ]
    90: 
    91:     if not valid_statuses:
    92:         return HEALTHY
    93: 
    94:     return max(
    95:         valid_statuses,
    96:         key=lambda status: GOVERNANCE_SEVERITY_ORDER[status],
    97:     )
    98: 
    99: 
   100: def score_for_status(status: str) -> int:
   101:     if status == HEALTHY:
   102:         return 100
   103:     if status == WARNING:
   104:         return 85
   105:     if status == STALE:
   106:         return 55
   107:     if status == DRIFTED:
   108:         return 30
   109:     if status == REPAIR_REQUIRED:
   110:         return 10
   111:     return 0

  1024: def is_datetime_newer(left: str | None, right: str | None) -> bool:
  1025:     left_dt = parse_governance_datetime(left)
  1026:     right_dt = parse_governance_datetime(right)
  1027: 
  1028:     if not left_dt or not right_dt:
  1029:         return False
  1030: 
  1031:     return left_dt > right_dt

  1249: def classify_stale_issue_severity(issue: GovernanceIssue) -> str:
  1250:     code = str(issue.code or "")
  1251: 
  1252:     info_codes = {

  1255:     }

  1274:         return "INFO"

   197:         active_ids = []
   198:

   218:             "entity_count": len(entities_by_doc.get(doc_id, set())),

   258: def build_cross_document_phrase_relationships(
   259:     workspace_id: str,
   260: ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
   261: 
   262:     registry_data = build_document_registry(workspace_id)
   263: 
   264:     docs = registry_data.get("documents", {})
   265: 
   266:     relationships: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
   267: 
   268:     doc_ids = sorted(docs.keys())
   269: 
   270:     for i in range(len(doc_ids)):
   271:         for j in range(i + 1, len(doc_ids)):
   272: 
   273:             left_id = doc_ids[i]
   274:             right_id = doc_ids[j]
   275: 
   276:             left_doc = docs.get(left_id, {})
   277:             right_doc = docs.get(right_id, {})
   278: 
   279:             left_phrases = set(left_doc.get("phrases", []))
   280:             right_phrases = set(right_doc.get("phrases", []))
   281: 
   282:             shared_phrases = sorted(left_phrases & right_phrases)

   581: def _same_domain_allowed(url: str, allowed_domain: str = "") -> bool:
   582:     if not allowed_domain:
   583:         return True
   584: 
   585:     try:
   586:         host = urlparse(str(url or "")).netloc.lower()
   587:         domain = str(allowed_domain or "").lower().replace("https://", "").replace("http://", "").strip("/")
   588:         return host == domain or host.endswith("." + domain)
   589:     except Exception:
   590:         return False

   288: 
   289: def website_completion_gate(
   290:     *,
   291:     workspace_id: str,
   292:     website_id: str,
   293:     page_jobs: List[Dict[str, Any]],
   294: ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
   295:     """
   296:     Website-level completion gate.
   297: 
   298:     A website is complete only after all discovered page jobs have reached
   299:     terminal states and no required page remains pending/running.
   300:     """
   301: 
   302:     ws = safe_id(workspace_id)
   303:     site = safe_id(website_id, "website")
   304: 
   305:     page_count = len(page_jobs)
   306:     status_counts = Counter()
   307: 
   308:     failed_pages: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
   309:     pending_pages: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
   310:     completed_pages: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
   311: 
   312:     terminal_statuses = {"completed", "failed", "dead_letter"}
   313: 
   314:     for job in page_jobs:
   315:         job_id = job.get("job_id", "")
   316:         status = read_job_status(ws, job_id)
   317:         state = status.get("status") or job.get("status") or "unknown"
   318: 
   319:         status_counts[state] += 1
   320: 
   321:         row = {
   322:             "job_id": job_id,
   323:             "job_type": job.get("job_type"),

   295:     "test",
   296:     "tmp",
   297:     "none",

   314: def _looks_like_noise_phrase(value: Any) -> bool:
   315:     text = _norm(value)
   316: 
   317:     if not text:
   318:         return True
   319: 
   320:     if text in _UPLOAD_NOISE_TERMS:
   321:         return True
   322: 
   323:     # paragraph/sentence IDs like p1_s2
   324:     if re.fullmatch(r"p\d+_s\d+", text):
   325:         return True
   326: 
   327:     # hashes / ids
   328:     if re.fullmatch(r"[a-f0-9]{16,}", text):
   329:         return True
   330: 
   331:     # uuid-like chunks
   332:     if re.fullmatch(r"[a-f0-9]{8,}[-_][a-f0-9]{4,}.*", text):
   333:         return True
   334: 
   335:     # mostly punctuation / underscores / digits
   336:     letters = re.findall(r"[a-z]", text)
   337:     if len(letters) < 3:
   338:         return True
   339: 
   340:     # single technical token with underscore
   341:     if " " not in text and "_" in text:
   342:         return True
   343: 
   344:     # too URL/file-like
   345:     if any(x in text for x in [".json", ".py", ".html", ".docx", "\\", "/"]):
   346:         return True
   347:

   383: def _passes_uploaded_quality_filter(value: Any) -> bool:
   384:     text = _norm(value)
   385: 
   386:     if _looks_like_noise_phrase(text):
   387:         return False
   388: 
   389:     words = re.findall(r"[a-z0-9]+", text)
   390: 
   391:     if len(words) >= 2:
   392:         return _uploaded_phrase_quality_score(text) >= 0.45
   393: 
   394:     # Keep single-token terms only if strong enough.
   395:     # Later entity/type support can promote more single-token concepts.
   396:     return _uploaded_phrase_quality_score(text) >= 0.65
   397: 
   398: 
   399: def load_uploaded_document_evidence(workspace_id: str) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
   400:     evidence: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
   401: 
   402:     files = _load_upload_json_candidates(workspace_id)
   403: 
   404:     for path in files:
   405:         obj = _read_json(path, None)
   406:         if obj is None:
   407:             continue
   408: 
   409:         phrases = _walk_strings(obj, limit=1500)
   410: 
   411:         for phrase in phrases:
   412:             if not phrase or not _passes_uploaded_quality_filter(phrase):
   413:                 continue
   414: 
   415:             quality = _uploaded_phrase_quality_score(phrase)
   416: 
   417:             evidence.append({
   418:                 "concept": phrase,
   419:                 "related_phrase": phrase,
   420:                 "relation_type": "uploaded_document_phrase",
   421:                 "source": "uploaded_documents",
   422:                 "confidence": round(0.70 + (quality * 0.10), 4),
   423:                 "evidence": {
   424:                     "file": str(path),
   425:                     "kind": path.name,
   426:                     "quality_score": quality,
   427:                 }
   428:             })

   440:     *,
   441:     workspace_id: str,

   443:     payload: Dict[str, Any] | None = None,
   444:     parent_job_id: str = "",
   445:     batch_id: str = "",
   446: ) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:

   468:         )
   469: 
   470:         jobs.append(job)
   471: 
   472:     return jobs

    27: def _read_json(path: Path, default: Any) -> Any:
    28:     try:
    29:         if not path.exists():
    30:             return default
    31:         return json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    32:     except Exception:
    33:         return default
    34: 
    35: 
    36: def _write_json_atomic(path: Path, obj: Any) -> None:
    37:     path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    38:     tmp = path.with_suffix(path.suffix + ".tmp")
    39:     tmp.write_text(json.dumps(obj, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
    40:     os.replace(tmp, path)
    41: 
    42: 
    43: def _norm_text(value: Any) -> str:
    44:     text = str(value or "").strip().lower()
    45:     text = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9\s\-]+", " ", text)
    46:     text = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", text)
    47:     return text.strip()

    56:     try:

    58:             json.dump(payload, f, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)

    60:     finally:
    61:         try:

    63:                 os.remove(tmp_path)

    61: # -------------------------
    62: # Parsing
    63: # Supports:
    64: # 1) URL-ish draft map (any lines containing URLs)
    65: # 2) CSV with header: topic_id, working_title, planned_slug, planned_url, aliases, priority, canonical
    66: # 3) Pipe format: topic_id|working_title|planned_slug|planned_url|aliases|priority|canonical
    67: # -------------------------
    68: def _parse_draft_text(text: str) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
    69:     lines = [l.strip() for l in (text or "").splitlines() if l.strip()]
    70:     if not lines:
    71:         return []
    72: 
    73:     # -------------------------
    74:     # URL-ish draft map support (tolerant)
    75:     # Extract first URL from each line (works for CSV, numbered lists, pipes, etc.)
    76:     # If >= 60% of lines contain a URL, treat as URL-only draft map.
    77:     # -------------------------
    78:     url_hits: List[str] = []
    79:     for line in lines:
    80:         m = re.search(r"(https?://\S+)", line, flags=re.I)
    81:         if m:
    82:             url_hits.append(m.group(1).rstrip('",)'))  # trim common trailing chars
    83: 
    84:     if url_hits and (len(url_hits) / max(1, len(lines)) >= 0.6):
    85:         out: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
    86:         seen = set()
    87: 
    88:         def clean_url(u: str) -> str:
    89:             u = (u or "").strip().strip('"')
    90:             u = u.split("#", 1)[0]
    91:             return u

   461: def _read_json(fp: Path, default: Any) -> Any:
   462:     try:
   463:         if not fp.exists():
   464:             return default
   465:         return json.loads(fp.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
   466:     except Exception:
   467:         return default
   468: 
   469: 
   470: def _write_json_atomic(fp: Path, obj: Any) -> None:
   471:     fp.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   472:     tmp = fp.with_suffix(fp.suffix + ".tmp")
   473:     tmp.write_text(json.dumps(obj, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
   474:     os.replace(tmp, fp)

   496: def _quality_score_for(source_type: str, repeats: int = 1) -> float:
   497:     base_map = {
   498:         "title": 1.00,
   499:         "heading_h1": 1.00,
   500:         "heading_h2": 0.95,

   509:         "alias": 0.60,
   510:     }
   511:     base = base_map.get(source_type, 0.65)
   512:     bonus = min(max(repeats - 1, 0) * 0.05, 0.20)
   513:     return round(min(base + bonus, 1.0), 3)

   205:     - Return ranked candidate URLs with evidence.
   206: 
   207:     Non-responsibilities:
   208:     - Does not crawl.
   209:     - Does not learn semantic meaning.
   210:     - Does not make final link decision.
   211:     - Does not insert editor links.
   212:     """
   213: 
   214:     if not understood_phrase.get("ready_for_target_discovery"):
   215:         return {
   216:             "ok": False,
   217:             "error": "phrase_not_ready_for_target_discovery",
   218:             "phrase_id": understood_phrase.get("phrase_id"),
   219:             "candidate_targets": [],
   220:         }
   221: 
   222:     active = _load_active_target_set(workspace_id)
   223:     if not active.get("ok"):
   224:         return {
   225:             "ok": False,
   226:             "error": active.get("error"),
   227:             "phrase_id": understood_phrase.get("phrase_id"),
   228:             "workspace_id": workspace_id,
   229:             "candidate_targets": [],
   230:             "active_target_set_path": active.get("path"),
   231:         }
   232: 
   233:     semantic_candidates = understood_phrase.get("semantic_match_candidates") or []
   234:     targets = active.get("items") or []
   235: 
   236:     ranked: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
   237: 
   238:     for target in targets:
   239:         best_score = 0.0
   240:         best_evidence: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None
   241: 
   242:         for candidate in semantic_candidates:
   243:             result = _score_candidate_against_target(candidate, target)
   244:             if result["score"] > best_score:
   245:                 best_score = result["score"]
   246:                 best_evidence = result["evidence"]
   247: 
   248:         if best_score > 0:
   249:             ranked.append({
   250:                 "url": target.get("url"),
   251:                 "title": target.get("title"),
   252:                 "slug": target.get("slug"),
   253:                 "topic_cluster": target.get("topic_cluster"),
   254:                 "section_cluster": target.get("section_cluster"),
   255:                 "source_pool": target.get("source_pool"),
   256:                 "retrieval_score": round(best_score, 4),
   257:                 "candidate_evidence": best_evidence or {},
   258:                 "target_record": target,
   259:             })
   260: 
   261:     ranked.sort(key=lambda x: x.get("retrieval_score", 0), reverse=True)
   262:     ranked = ranked[: max(1, int(limit or 10))]

    17: ("how to calculate ...").
    18: 
    19: This version fixes the asymmetry that makes an extractor universal:
    20: 
    21:   * VERBS are a (mostly) closed, niche-independent class -> we keep a broad
    22:     verb lexicon and gate structurally on it.
    23:   * NOUNS are open and vary by niche -> we never require a head to be in a

    25:     head; otherwise an unknown content word defaults to a valid head.

    28: extractor behaves the same for cooking, legal, automotive, gaming, finance,

   194: 
   195: def _phrase_candidates(item: Dict[str, Any]) -> Set[str]:
   196:     """
   197:     Universal canonical phrase extractor for topic clustering.
   198:     Uses titles/slugs to produce stable 2-3 word topic phrases.
   199:     Avoids sliding-window loops like "sleep regression sleep".
   200:     """
   201:     raw_parts: List[str] = []
   202: 
   203:     for k in ("title", "h1", "label"):
   204:         val = str(item.get(k) or "").strip()
   205:         if val:
   206:             raw_parts.append(val)
   207: 
   208:     path = str(item.get("path") or "")
   209:     if path:
   210:         raw_parts.append(path.replace("/", " ").replace("-", " ").replace("_", " "))
   211: 
   212:     for k in ("matched_phrases", "aliases"):
   213:         vals = item.get(k) or []
   214:         if isinstance(vals, list):
   215:             raw_parts.extend(str(v or "") for v in vals if str(v or "").strip())
   216: 
   217:     out: Set[str] = set()
   218: 
   219:     for raw in raw_parts:
   220:         clean = re.sub(r"\.aspx\b", " ", str(raw), flags=re.I)
   221:         clean = re.sub(r"\b\d+\b", " ", clean)
   222:         toks = _dedupe_consecutive_tokens(_tokens(clean))
   223: 
   224:         if len(toks) < 2:
   225:             continue
   226: 
   227:         # Prefer first meaningful 2-word and 3-word title phrases.
   228:         for n in (2, 3):
   229:             if len(toks) >= n:
   230:                 phrase = " ".join(toks[:n]).strip()
   231:                 if not _is_bad_phrase_label(phrase):
   232:                     out.add(phrase)
   233: 
   234:         # Also allow adjacent phrase pairs where both tokens are meaningful.
   235:         for i in range(0, max(0, len(toks) - 1)):
   236:             phrase = " ".join(toks[i:i+2]).strip()

CODE: The public function `extract_smart_phrases(...)` keeps the same signature and
------------------------------------------------------------
     8: Why the previous version produced "hanging" phrases
     9: ---------------------------------------------------
    10: The old extractor slid fixed 2/3/4-word windows across a token stream and then
    11: tried to *reject* the bad ones with several hundred hand-written blocklists and
    12: regexes. Sliding windows inherently slice through the middle of grammatical
    13: constituents, so "calculate the fertile window" becomes "calculate the",
    14: "the fertile", "fertile window", etc. The blocklists can never enumerate every
    15: truncation, so fragments leak through.
    16: 
    17: This version flips the approach: instead of cutting arbitrary windows and
    18: filtering, it (1) chunks each sentence into whole noun-phrase / verb-object
    19: constituents, then (2) trims both ends down to content-word boundaries and
    20: rejects anything that still starts or ends on a function word. A phrase is kept
    21: only if it begins and ends on a content word and ends on a noun-like head. That
    22: single structural rule removes essentially all "hanging" output.
    23: 
    24: It prefers spaCy or NLTK if installed (best accuracy) and otherwise falls back
    25: to a self-contained heuristic chunker, so it has **no required dependencies**.
    26: 
    27: The public function `extract_smart_phrases(...)` keeps the same signature and
    28: output shape as before, so this is a drop-in replacement.
    29: """

   229:     }
   230: 
   231: 
   232: def rank_document_registry_targets(
   233:     phrase: str,
   234:     workspace_id: str,
   235:     limit: int = 10,
   236:     exclude_document_id: Optional[str] = None,
   237: ) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
   238:     targets = load_document_registry_targets(workspace_id)
   239:     ranked: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
   240: 
   241:     for target in targets:
   242:         if exclude_document_id and str(target.get("document_id") or "") == str(exclude_document_id):
   243:             continue
   244: 
   245:         payload = runtime_safe_payload(phrase, target)
   246:         if payload["allowed"]:
   247:             ranked.append(payload)
   248: 
   249:     ranked.sort(key=lambda x: x.get("score", 0), reverse=True)
   250:     return ranked[:limit]
   251:

   605:                     doc_id=doc_id, workspace_id=workspace_id, vertical=vertical,
   606:                     full_text=full_text, heading_level=None,
   607:                 )

    75: def _display_text(item: Dict[str, Any]) -> str:

    81: def extract_phrase_candidates(active_phrase_pool: Any) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
    82:     """Extract candidate dicts from any of the known active-pool shapes."""
    83:     candidates: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
    84:     if not active_phrase_pool:
    85:         return candidates
    86: 
    87:     raw = None
    88:     if isinstance(active_phrase_pool, dict):
    89:         raw = (active_phrase_pool.get("phrases")
    90:                or active_phrase_pool.get("items")
    91:                or active_phrase_pool.get("candidates"))
    92:     elif isinstance(active_phrase_pool, list):
    93:         raw = active_phrase_pool
    94: 
    95:     if isinstance(raw, dict):
    96:         for key, payload in raw.items():
    97:             if isinstance(payload, dict):
    98:                 item = dict(payload)
    99:                 item.setdefault("phrase", key)
   100:                 candidates.append(item)
   101:             else:
   102:                 candidates.append({"phrase": key, "value": payload})
   103:     elif isinstance(raw, list):
   104:         for payload in raw:
   105:             if isinstance(payload, dict):
   106:                 candidates.append(dict(payload))
   107:             elif isinstance(payload, str):
   108:                 candidates.append({"phrase": payload})
   109:     return candidates
   110:

   117:     return _WS_RE.sub(" ", str(article_text or "").lower())

    16: def link_site_pages_to_unified_content_v1(*, workspace_id: str, site_pages_path: str | None=None) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    17:     path = Path(site_pages_path) if site_pages_path else _site_pages_path_v1(workspace_id)

    19:         raise FileNotFoundError(f'Site pages file not found: {path}')

    37:     data['updated_at'] = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
    38:     path.write_text(json.dumps(data, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding='utf-8')

   593: def _host_matches_domain(url: str, domain: str) -> bool:
   594:     try:
   595:         host = urlparse(str(url or "")).netloc.lower().strip()
   596:         host = host[4:] if host.startswith("www.") else host
   597:         dom = str(domain or "").lower().strip()
   598:         dom = dom[4:] if dom.startswith("www.") else dom
   599:         return bool(host and dom and (host == dom or host.endswith("." + dom)))
   600:     except Exception:
   601:         return False
